A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DynamicNER and CascadeNER. All 25 pages of each version, including Appendices A–Q, provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v6 reports original DynamicNER evaluations in Section 5, external-benchmark experiments in Appendix E, ablations in Appendix F, and annotation-agreement results in Appendix K.

after.justification: v7 retains these original experimental and data-analysis results, including benchmark scores, ablations, and annotation-agreement measurements.

M1.justification: The four-stage dynamic categorization procedure and CascadeNER’s extraction, result fusion, contextual classification, and progressive granularity handling remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same eight-language DynamicNER coverage and the same external benchmarks: CoNLL2003, CrossNER, FewNERD, PAN-X, and MultiCoNER. No task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same baselines, including XLM-RoBERTa, GPT-NER, PromptNER, and Appendix E’s task-specific ACE+document-context, BERT-MRC+DSC, and GEMNET comparisons. Removing the duplicate table removes no comparator.

E3.justification: Data splits, sampling procedures, evaluation metrics, model backbones, three-shot demonstrations, extraction repetition counts, and training settings are unchanged. The revised citation supporting F1 does not change the metric.

E4.justification: The granularity comparisons, categorization-quality analyses, extraction-repetition and contextual-classification ablations, and annotation-agreement audit are retained unchanged. Appendix F’s tables are renumbered and repositioned.

E5.justification: Both versions report five independent tests for random categorization and 500 bootstrap resamples for English/Chinese 95% confidence intervals. Appendix G’s uncertainty reporting is unchanged; its table changes from Table 12 to Table 11.

E6.justification: All unique results are retained with unchanged values. Removed v6 Table 8 duplicates retained Table 7, including CascadeNER’s few-shot F1 scores of 92.8 on CoNLL2003 and 75.9 on FewNERD-66. The multilingual results move from v6 Table 9 to v7 Table 8 unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 and their associated mathematical definitions and reasoning remain unchanged, including result fusion, hierarchical classification, categorization metrics, and stratified sampling.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about DynamicNER’s dynamic categorization and CascadeNER’s accuracy and computational efficiency.

C2.justification: Interpretations of generalization, granularity, efficiency, and baseline behavior are unchanged. Qualifications concerning flat-NER evaluation, language coverage, dataset size, nested entities, and contamination are also retained.

D1.justification: Implementation, annotation, filtering, hardware, LoRA hyperparameters, prompts, and code/data access information remain unchanged. Appendix L’s hyperparameter table is only renumbered from Table 15 to Table 14.

R1.justification: The Dice-loss reference is revised to match the Li et al. work already listed, producing 2020a/2020b entries and corresponding citation labels. This is a bibliographic revision; related-work coverage and research positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: Bibliographic details, author-year citations, table cross-references, and the arXiv version/date stamp are updated. The substantive prose and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v7 removes the small duplicate Table 8 while retaining Table 7, renumbers subsequent tables, and reflows the appendices. Several tables move closer to their discussion, and Figure 11 moves from PDF page 23 to page 22 without changing its content.

improvement.justification: Removing the redundant table and placing the classification-ablation and confidence-interval tables on the pages discussing them modestly improves appendix readability without losing evidence. The bibliography revision still leaves duplicate Li et al. 2020a/2020b entries. The overall gain is editorial; scientific content and evidential strength remain unchanged.
